ModMetaData.name: Cheat Traits
ModMetaData.author: nalroff
ModMetaData.description:
Cheat Traits adds 17 overpowered, role-focused traits for custom colonists and hero pawns.
Each Ch* trait pushes a pawn into a clear specialty: unarmed brawler, revolver ace, speedster, tank, master grower, master crafter, master builder, miracle doctor, alchemist cook, beastmaster, diplomat, miner, spellcaster, battlefield bard, and more.
None of these traits are pure stat monsters--each trait has a unique ability or building that makes the pawn feel like a hero in their role. For example:
- Green Thumb supercharges nearby plant growth and unlocks the Floragen Core. - Comfy extinguishes nearby fires and unlocks the power-free Comfort Node. - Tesla unlocks Tesla Coils that generate power and chain-zap nearby hostiles, stun-locking mechanoids while sparing raiders for capture. - Alchemist turns meals into timed buffs and unlocks the Alchemy Cauldron for brewing Trail Tonic. - Ascendant researches at incredible speed and unlocks the Eureka Forge, which periodically grants normally-unattainable crafting recipes. - Ascendant, Beastmaster, Diplomat, and Bard project powerful support auras.
The mod also adds 14 custom castable abilities granted by traits — all cooldown-based and built without Royalty (no psylink or psyfocus needed). These include Flying Punch, Deadeye, Blink, Iron Wall, Reforge, Retrofit, Miracle Heal, Tunnel, Call of the Wild, Bond Pawns, and the Wizard's spellbook of Lightning Bolt, map-wide Teleport Other, Mass Berserk, and Super Soldier.
This mod is aimed at players who want standout specialists, themed runs, or unapologetically strong pawns. The traits use commonality 0 by default, so they are best suited for curated starts, custom pawn setups, or other deliberate trait assignment.
Prefer a wilder run? Mod Settings include a commonality slider (global, plus optional per-trait overrides) that lets the cheat traits roll randomly on any generated pawn — your colonists, allies, and even raiders. It stays off by default.
